think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 28-year-old Vietnamese immigrant on biologic therapy (anti-TNF monoclonal antibody adalimumab) for extensive plaque psoriasis, who presents with subacute fevers, dry cough, myalgias, and transient partial response to empirical antibiotics. Despite prior completion of a 9-month isoniazid preventive regimen years earlier, chest and abdominal CT demonstrate a 1.1 cm lung nodule, moderate pleural effusion, hilar adenopathy, ascites, and diffuse peritoneal and omental nodularity. The central tension is distinguishing disseminated mycobacterial infection (severe breakthrough reactivation under TNF blockade) from atypical community-acquired bacterial pleuropneumonia, systemic endemic mycosis, and diffuse peritoneal carcinomatosis / lymphoma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical presentation includes demographics (28-year-old man, emigrated from Vietnam 11 years prior, healthcare worker, nonsmoker), past medical history (extensive plaque psoriasis treated with subcutaneous adalimumab for over 2 years, completed 9 months of isoniazid chemoprophylaxis in 2004 after household contact with a relative treated for pulmonary infection), presentation chronology (2 months of low-grade fever, myalgias, severe dry cough, transient improvement with doxycycline/azithromycin), initial clinic vitals and clear pulmonary exam, outpatient clear CXR 3 weeks prior, chest CT findings (1.1 cm RLL lobular opacity, right pleural effusion, hilar adenopathy, perihepatic/perisplenic ascites), admission vitals (temperature 39°C, BP 121/87, HR 95, RR 22, SpO2 97%), exam findings (bilateral pulmonary crackles, diffuse psoriatic rash), and abdominopelvic CT findings (diffuse nodularity of the omentum and peritoneal lining with ascites). The breakpoint stops immediately prior to invasive diagnostic procedures (thoracentesis, pleural fluid ADA, bronchoscopy, percutaneous peritoneal biopsy, and laparoscopy).
3. Differential Distinctions: Atypical bacterial pneumonia with parapneumonic effusion can explain cough, fever, and temporary response to macrolides/tetracyclines, but cannot account for diffuse omental nodularity, ascites, and persistent high fever. Peritoneal carcinomatosis or lymphoma is a major concern in a young immunosuppressed patient presenting with polyserositis and omental caking, but pleural fluid ADA elevation and granulomatous histology rule out malignancy. Endemic systemic fungal infections (histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis) occur under anti-TNF therapy, but cultures yield Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.
case_prompt:
A 28-year-old male healthcare worker who emigrated from Vietnam 11 years ago presents with a two-month history of fevers, generalized myalgias, and a severe nonproductive cough. He has a history of extensive plaque psoriasis for which he has been treated with subcutaneous adalimumab for over two years. His grandfather had been treated for a severe chronic pulmonary infection in Vietnam 15 years prior, and the patient had completed a nine-month course of isoniazid chemoprophylaxis in 2004. Approximately one month prior to evaluation, he received courses of doxycycline and azithromycin, which resulted in only temporary symptomatic improvement. He is a nonsmoker, has no pets, and has never received the pneumococcal vaccine.

An outpatient evaluation by a pulmonologist three weeks prior included unremarkable blood tests and a normal plain chest radiograph. On evaluation in the clinic, he is non-toxic with a temperature of 37.2°C, blood pressure of 109/73 mmHg, heart rate of 85 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 14 breaths per minute, with clear breath sounds bilaterally. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest performed that day demonstrates a 1.1 cm lobular opacity in the right lower lobe, a moderate right pleural effusion, hilar lymphadenopathy, and a small volume of perihepatic and perisplenic ascites.

He is promptly admitted to the hospital. On admission, his temperature is 39.0°C, blood pressure is 121/87 mmHg, heart rate is 95 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 97% on ambient air. Physical examination reveals bilateral pulmonary crackles and extensive active psoriatic plaques. A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals diffuse nodularity and thickening of the omentum and peritoneal lining associated with ascites.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute onset of cough, fevers, and temporary improvement after empiric doxycycline and azithromycin; however, symptoms recurred with progression to polyserositis and extensive peritoneal and omental nodularity unresponsive to standard antibacterials.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient had been treated with a course of doxycycline followed by azithromycin approximately one month earlier, causing temporary improvement in his symptoms.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the diffuse omental caking, peritoneal nodular studding, and exudative polyserositis in a patient receiving chronic immunosuppressive biologic therapy; however, histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis performed with intravenous contrast revealed diffuse nodularity of the omentum and peritoneal lining (Figure 2), raising the concern for tuberculous peritonitis (TBP).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Pulmonary and Peritoneal Tuberculosis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Diagnostic thoracentesis revealed an exudative lymphocytic effusion with markedly elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA 110.3 U/L), peritoneal biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli on Fite's stain, and tissue cultures definitively isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The pleural fluid was exudative with an 80% lymphocytic predominance. No acid fast bacilli (AFB) were seen. The pleural fluid adenosine deaminase (ADA) was elevated at 110.3 u/L... Growth of MTB complex was noted from the percutaneous peritoneal biopsy after 16 days, and subsequently all other culture specimens showed growth by day 30.

editor_comments: Standardized admission diagnostic case for disseminated (pulmonary and peritoneal) tuberculosis occurring under TNF-alpha inhibitor therapy despite remote latent TB prophylaxis. Admission breakpoint established prior to thoracentesis and peritoneal biopsies.
